method: Volume load, also called tonnage, counts the external work of a strength set as the load multiplied by the reps. One set of five at 100 kg therefore carries 500 kg of volume, five such sets in a session carry 2,500 kg, and three sessions a week carry 7,500 kg. Reps are counted the same way: reps per set multiplied by sets gives reps per session, and that multiplied by sessions gives reps per week. Relative volume divides the weekly total by bodyweight, so 7,500 kg a week at 80 kg bodyweight is 93.75 times bodyweight; it is reported only when a bodyweight is entered, and the same unit is assumed for load and bodyweight. The load must be 0.5-1000 in the selected unit with at most two decimals, reps 1-100, sets per session 1-20 and sessions per week 1-14, all whole numbers; bodyweight is optional and must be 20-400 when given, and anything malformed or out of range is refused with a specific message rather than parsed loosely. Only the external load is counted: the lifter's own body mass, band or machine assistance, sled friction and any warm-up sets the user does not enter are excluded, and one lift is handled at a time, so a full session is the sum of its separate entries. The tool reports arithmetic on the user's own entries and does not assess whether a load, rep range, set count or weekly frequency is suitable, does not estimate fatigue, adaptation, injury risk or progress, and is not coaching or medical advice. It also does not log, store or compare sessions over time. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Volume load in strength training is conventionally sets x reps x load, reported in the load's own unit.
Training-volume reviews report weekly volume load and volume relative to bodyweight as summary measures of resistance-training work.
Session volume load is the sum of the volume load of the individual sets, so per-set volume times the number of sets.
Bodyweight, band assistance and machine assistance are separate from the external load placed on the bar or stack.
